item.title: [github_trending] pingdotgg/t3code
item.description: T3 Code is an open-source control surface from pingdotgg for the coding agents already installed and authenticated on your machine, shipping as iOS, Android, web and Electron desktop clients. It drives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity and fx on your existing subscriptions. The authors say Codex's desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass didn't meet their bar, so the code stays forkable. Useful for developers juggling several agent subscriptions

item.description: A Juejin post works through a question that interviewers now ask: given that candidates are assumed to use AI, why should a company still hire you when AI already writes most of the code? The author contrasts this with interviews from two years ago, which still tested hand-written Promises and React Fiber internals, and argues the evaluation criteria have shifted. Useful for developers preparing for technical interviews right now.

item.title: [infoq] 写好的 Skill 如何让整个团队复用？Snowflake CoCo 打通共享与治理流程 ｜ 技术实践
item.description: Snowflake has shipped a preview feature for its CoCo agent (formerly Cortex Code) that turns local SKILL.md playbooks into account-wide, shareable and version-managed objects built on a native SQL type called Cortex Extension. Teams can share skills by link, browse a shared catalog, and admins can certify trusted ones. The article walks through writing, sharing, discovery and certification, showing the SQL behind each step.

Working with a reimbursement budget of only about 20 dollars, he is weighing Cursor as a substitute and says he still prefers Opus. item.title: [v2ex] [推广] MiroFish：把产品发布、用户反应等问题做成多角色情景推演
item.description: MiroFish.work is a browser-based multi-agent simulator for scenario planning. You describe target users, the existing alternative, pricing and constraints, pose a concrete question such as what happens if the free quota shrinks, then run role-based reactions and read a report of assumptions, disagreements and likely outcomes. The author warns results depend on inputs and model assumptions and should be weighed alongside interviews, experiments or business data.

item.title: [infoq] 从近两小时到 30 秒，SQL 查询性能优化有了新解法 ｜ 技术实践
item.description: Snowflake's Optima Planning now matches at a finer grain than whole queries: it hashes plan fragments and individual operators such as a specific join, so execution feedback from one query can speed up structurally similar queries that have never run before. In one production case at a large healthcare technology company, a 19-join analytical query dropped from nearly two hours to 30 seconds. The system also checks whether reused feedback would over-generalize before applying it.

item.title: [juejin] Cursor 转 Codex 大半个月，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: The author writes up roughly half a month of using Codex after switching from Cursor: Cursor was what first made AI-assisted coding feel striking, while Codex comes across as a full agent that pushes tasks forward on its own rather than just a coding assistant. Aimed at developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt, or whether switching workflows is worth it.

item.title: [infoq] CI 出错后，谁来把关？Buildkite 的智能体新思路
item.description: Buildkite now offers pipeline-scoped secrets that can be narrowed by branch, queue, build source or creator, with values staying hidden after creation. Its open-source MCP server gains validate_pipeline, which checks pipeline YAML against Buildkite's schema without uploading a file, and compare_builds, which diffs a failed run against the last successful one on the same branch. Agent v4.1.0 extends OpenTelemetry data. Aimed at platform engineers who own CI credentials and failure triage.

item.description: vercel-labs released agent-desktop, a CLI and C library that lets AI agents read and drive desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree on macOS, Windows and Linux. Apache-2.0 licensed and published on npm, it targets developers wiring GUI automation into agents.

It has zero external dependencies: an .sgmodule defines the panel and an ES5 script talks to Tailscale API v2, refreshing every 300 seconds and pruning duplicate offline nodes along the way. Source is on GitHub.

item.title: [infoq] 66 岁 Yann LeCun 发新论文挑战 Scaling Law：1.09 亿参数胜过 720 亿，模型越大不一定越懂世界
item.description: On October 29, Yann LeCun and Brown University's Randall Balestriero published a 37-page paper arguing that models trained independently on different modalities can, under certain conditions, learn mutually aligned world representations. A 109M-parameter text JEPA beat Qwen2.5-72B and Llama-3-70B on cross-modal alignment while needing 21.6M training samples, versus 900M for next-token prediction models.

item.title: [infoq] TornadoVM 7 支持 Java 应用程序运行原生 GPU 工作负载
item.description: TornadoVM 7.3 ships as an open-source framework that offloads Java code onto GPUs and multi-core CPUs inside existing JDKs. The release replaces JNI with the Foreign Function & Memory API, drops the experimental JVMCI dependency, adds cuTile support and direct cuBLAS/CUTLASS calls from TaskGraphs on the CUDA backend, and introduces multi-GPU execution across JDK 21, 25, 26 and 27. Developers with data-parallel loops are the main audience.

item.title: [infoq] 别再迷信 Agent 的自主性了
item.description: An InfoQ live panel with engineers from Fliggy, Huolala and Jiangsu Mobile debated where to draw the autonomy boundary for enterprise agents. The shared view: transaction paths need determinism, so ordering, dispatching and wallet-related actions stay behind rules or human approval, while models handle intent clarification and long-tail phrasing. The real moat is a company's own data, tools and evaluation pipeline, not an answer that merely looks plausible.

The author is moving all his servers off Ubuntu and calls out Canonical's 'timely patches' marketing.

item.title: [juejin] 手机到底有没有偷听我们？我抓包了 72 小时，抓到了真凶
item.description: A developer captured 72 hours of phone traffic and found zero microphone wake-ups at the hardware level, which weakens the "my phone is listening" theory. The uncanny precognition instead traces to public NAT spatio-temporal hypergraphs (ST-GNN), modern private set intersection (PSI), and on-device micro-model feature vectorization. Useful for engineers who want to understand how targeting actually works and where the privacy line sits.

item.title: [hackernews] Postgres 19 is late because so many more bugs are being found now
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 will most likely slip to November rather than the usual mid-September to mid-October window, according to major contributor Robert Haas, because far more bugs are turning up during beta, a shift he blames on LLMs. Several large features, including SQL/PGQ and UPDATE/DELETE FOR PORTION OF, were reverted between late August and mid-September. Haas, a staff engineer at Databricks, walks through what that means for the release process.

item.title: [github_trending] JustVugg/colibri
item.description: colibri is a pure-C, dependency-free inference engine for mixture-of-experts models. Since an MoE model only activates a small slice of its experts per token, colibri keeps that slice in RAM and streams the remaining experts from disk, letting a machine you already own run open models with hundreds of billions of parameters. It targets developers who want large MoE inference without a dependency stack, and the README ships in several languages.
